record.original_question: Can one prove non-integrability of the two-dimensional Euler equation, in the sense that the equation fails at least one appropriate notion of integrability for infinite-dimensional Hamiltonian systems despite having Casimirs and a Lax-type form?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the two-dimensional incompressible Euler equation on a closed surface (for instance the two-torus $\mathbb{T}^2$ or the two-sphere $S^2$) with area form $\mu$. In vorticity form it reads
$$\partial_t \omega + \{\psi, \omega\} = 0, \qquad \Delta \psi = \omega, \qquad \int \omega\,\mu = 0,$$
where $\omega$ is the vorticity, $\psi$ the stream function and $\{\cdot,\cdot\}$ the Poisson bracket induced by $\mu$. This equation is the Hamiltonian flow on the dual of the Lie algebra $\mathrm{svect}(M)$ of divergence-free vector fields, with Hamiltonian $H(\omega) = \tfrac12 \int \psi\,\omega\,\mu$. It admits the infinite family of Casimir functionals $C_f(\omega) = \int f(\omega)\,\mu$ for any smooth $f$, and may be written in Lax form $\dot L = [L, A]$ for suitable operators $L, A$ on the surface.

Prove that, despite possessing this Lax-type representation and the infinite family of Casimirs, the two-dimensional Euler equation is non-integrable as an infinite-dimensional Hamiltonian system, in the sense that it fails at least one appropriate notion of complete integrability (for example, the absence of a complete commuting family of analytic first integrals independent of the Casimirs that would foliate generic coadjoint orbits by invariant tori, or the non-existence of action-angle coordinates on generic symplectic leaves).
artifact.status_search_result: The non-integrability of the 2D Euler equation as an infinite-dimensional Hamiltonian system is widely conjectured but, to current knowledge, not rigorously established. Available literature confirms its non-canonical Hamiltonian structure, the existence of Casimirs (vorticity moments), and Lax-type formulations, while only conjecturing the absence of additional conserved quantities beyond energy and momenta. No source verifies a proof of non-integrability in a rigorous infinite-dimensional sense.

status_evidence.title: Integrability structures of the (2+1)-dimensional Euler equation
status_evidence.snippet: A local variational Poisson structure for the 2D Euler equation is constructed; the question of complete integrability remains open and is discussed only at the level of structures, not of a proof of non-integrability.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work studies integrability structures (Hamiltonian, symplectic, Lax-type) of 2D Euler without establishing non-integrability.

status_evidence.title: A Nonlinear Hamiltonian Structure for the Euler Equations
status_evidence.snippet: Conjectures that no further conservation laws exist beyond energy and linear and angular momenta, indicating Euler equations are not completely integrable.
status_evidence.claim: Non-integrability of Euler is stated as a conjecture, not a theorem.

status_evidence.title: Symplectic methods for isospectral flows and 2D ideal hydrodynamics
status_evidence.snippet: Connections between geometric mechanics, statistical mechanics and integrability theory are explored numerically; the system is treated as non-integrable based on numerical/structural evidence.
status_evidence.claim: Numerical and geometric studies treat 2D Euler as non-integrable but do not provide a rigorous proof.
